subject: internals of scale.model = TRUE for RW1 model

messages.author: 6b3dfa6c2646a8c1
messages.subject: internals of scale.model = TRUE for RW1 model
parts:
Hello, 

I am trying to understand how the scale.model option is implemented for a RW1 model. The scaling of the Q matrix that I get is not consistent with what I had expected based on applying inla.scale.model() to the RW1 structure matrix.

In the below example where the precision is fixed to be 1, I had expected the matrix returned by misc$configs$config[[1]]$Q to be the same as the Qscaled calculated by inla.scale.model() (except for the top right term):

> library(INLA)
>
> df <- data.frame(x = 1, y = NA)
>
> Q <- t(diff(diag(4))) %*% diff(diag(4))
> Qscaled <- inla.scale.model(Q, constr = list(A = matrix(1, ncol = 4), e = 0))
>
> fit_scaled <- inla(y ~ 0 + f(x, model = "rw1", scale.model= TRUE, values = 1:4,
+                              hyper = list(prec = list(initial = 0, fixed = TRUE))),
+                    data = df,
+                    control.inla = list(int.strategy = "eb"),
+                    control.compute = list(config = TRUE))
>
> fit_scaled$misc$configs$config[[1]]$Q[-1, -1]
4 x 4 sparse Matrix of class "dgCMatrix"
                                              
[1,] 162755.2 -0.4494161  .          .        
[2,]      .    0.8988424 -0.4494161  .        
[3,]      .    .          0.8988424 -0.4494161
[4,]      .    .          .          0.4494263
>
> Qscaled
4 x 4 sparse Matrix of class "dgTMatrix"
                                                
[1,]  0.5728219 -0.5728219  .          .        
[2,] -0.5728219  1.1456439 -0.5728219  .        
[3,]  .         -0.5728219  1.1456439 -0.5728219
[4,]  .          .         -0.5728219  0.5728219
> 


If I set scale.model = FALSE, then misc$configs$config[[1]]$Q returns the RW1 structure matrix, as I'd expected:

> fit_unscaled <- inla(y ~ 0 + f(x, model = "rw1", scale.model= FALSE, values = 1:4, diagonal = 0,
+                                hyper = list(prec = list(initial = 0, fixed = TRUE))),
+                      data = df,
+                      control.inla = list(int.strategy = "eb"),
+                      control.compute = list(config = TRUE))
>
> fit_unscaled$misc$configs$config[[1]]$Q[-1, -1]
4 x 4 sparse Matrix of class "dgCMatrix"
                      
[1,] 162755.8 -1  .  .
[2,]      .    2 -1  .
[3,]      .    .  2 -1
[4,]      .    .  .  1
>
> Q
     [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4]
[1,]    1   -1    0    0
[2,]   -1    2   -1    0
[3,]    0   -1    2   -1
[4,]    0    0   -1    1


Also, if I use model = "besag" rather than model = "rw1", the Q matrix from misc$configs$config[[1]]$Q matches Qscaled:

> adj <- -Q + diag(diag(Q))
> fit_besag <- inla(y ~ 0 + f(x, model = "besag", scale.model= TRUE, graph = adj, diagonal = 0,
+                             hyper = list(prec = list(initial = 0, fixed = TRUE))),
+                      data = df,
+                      control.inla = list(int.strategy = "eb"),
+                      control.compute = list(config = TRUE))
>
> fit_besag$misc$configs$config[[1]]$Q[-1, -1]
4 x 4 sparse Matrix of class "dgCMatrix"
                                           
[1,] 162755.4 -0.572822  .         .       
[2,]      .    1.145644 -0.572822  .       
[3,]      .    .         1.145644 -0.572822
[4,]      .    .         .         0.572822
>
> Qscaled
4 x 4 sparse Matrix of class "dgTMatrix"
                                                
[1,]  0.5728219 -0.5728219  .          .        
[2,] -0.5728219  1.1456439 -0.5728219  .        
[3,]  .         -0.5728219  1.1456439 -0.5728219
[4,]  .          .         -0.5728219  0.5728219


Can you explain why the scaling of of the RW1 model is different than the result of scaling the structure matrix by inla.scale.model()?  Attached is the script I used for the above examples in case useful. As ever, many thanks for your advice.

Thanks,
Jeff

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] internals of scale.model = TRUE for RW1 model
parts:
Thanks Jeff,

you have a valid point. The issue was that the RW1 (and similar with
RW2) was using the code for a continuously defined spline, and treating
this as a continous in time process is slightly different from treating
it as a discrete process (like defined on 1,2,...,n.) and when the
correction is done, then its slightly different (like at the boundary),
and this difference make a difference especially for low dimension.

I changed the code, so the correction will coincide with the discrete
case, when the locations are eqvidistant. It's the right thing to do.

https://bitbucket.org/hrue/r-inla/commits/2f3b6374b6ca1014bc02a7ecbd96c239165aaaeb

attached is the new output and I attach the modified test code.
There are internal functions

INLA:::inla.rw1(n, scale.model)
INLA:::inla.rw2(n, scale.model)

you can use to get these matrices and scaling. its always a little
tricky to get the 'boundary' correct.

I'll build a new version of the package tonight.

thx again for pointing this out and for your code, which made it all
much simpler to locate and fix the issue.

H
